pageCache.pageTitle: Our Ethos | Private School London | Roche School
pageCache.text:
The Roche Approach
A global family
At The Roche School, we see ourselves as part of a global family, proud to embrace a rich diversity of languages and cultures which is truly reflective of London, a leading world city with a distinctly international identity. In 2025, our school was honoured to receive the British Council International School Award and we have the distinction of being the only primary school in London with a particular focus on Spanish language and learning. This commitment to bilingual learning and engagement with the wider world is an example of the Roche Approach principle of Open-mindedness in action.
A forest school experience in London
Our pupils enjoy visiting London’s world-class museums, galleries and historic sites, but our situation here in Wandsworth also allows for ready access to London’s phenomenal green spaces. Our children have the advantage of participating in regular Forest School lessons held in beautiful Wimbledon Common and in Richmond Park, a stunning national nature reserve. Lessons which foster a deeper connection with the natural world are just one expression of our commitment to the Roche Approach principles of Respect and Compassion.
A Montessori-style approach to learning in the early years
Children in our Nursery and Reception classes benefit from a careful balance of Montessori-style teaching and learning integrated with the National Curriculum for the Early Years and Foundation Stage. Free-flow, play-based learning is thoughtfully combined with engaging discrete teaching sessions led by our highly experienced teaching team.

pageCache.pageTitle: About us | Prep School London | Roche School
pageCache.text:
A truly independent school
Our roots
Our proprietor, Carmen Roche, established the school in 1983 with the intention of providing “a thorough education in a homely environment” and we have stayed true to that clear and honest ethos for over 40 years. The homely feel of our school is one of the first things visitors remark upon when they come to our school.
Members of the Roche family continue to live locally and their commitment to serving the children of the Wandsworth community is personal and heart-felt. Indeed, Sophie Roche is now the second generation of the Roche family to join our talented team of dedicated teachers and continues to champion the needs of each individual child in our school.
We place the child at the centre of everything we do at The Roche School. We are committed to an ethos of inclusivity, offering a warm welcome to children with a range of talents and abilities. We pride ourselves on being ambitious for every child: stretching and challenging them to be their very best selves.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from Our Head Teacher | Private School | Roche School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to The Roche School, an independent primary and nursery school offering a broad, aspirational education in a community which is warm, friendly and diverse – reflective of the wonderful city in which we live and conscious of the power of global citizenship. Our curriculum is taught by inspiring staff who ensure that pupils fully exceed expectations whilst they are with us – intellectually, creatively and in sporting terms. Attitudes to learning are important: we encourage pupils to enjoy challenge whether they are working together or independently, and we embed principles of growth mindset. This fosters sophisticated learning behaviours, such as resilience and introspection, that will take them to great success in senior school and beyond. We run small classes with children benefitting from high levels of personal attention and challenge.
We care about what we teach and how we teach it, with high-quality continued professional development for our staff, and we are proud of our strong academic record with pupils gaining places at top London secondary schools. In addition to the core curriculum, Art, Drama, Sport, Music, Humanities and Modern Foreign Languages are highly valued, as well as Forest School for Lower School and Philosophy 4 Children. Our Spanish Bilingual Stream is unique in London, and we foster an outward-looking international perspective in all our pupils. We also offer a wealth of extra-curricular activities in the form of over 40 after-school clubs. We seek strong parent partnerships and communicate regularly on a wide range of issues relevant to modern families.
The lively cultural mix at the school (complete with a non-gender bias approach) places an emphasis on respect and understanding. Thus, the atmosphere at the school is one of emotional intelligence and empowerment. Strong, comprehensive pastoral care and The Roche Approach emphasise our core values of kindness and respect towards others whilst we undertake this exciting and aspirational educational journey. We are interested in developing the individuality of every child, equipping our pupils with the deep rooted interpersonal and academic strengths they will need throughout their lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art, Music & Drama | Private School London | Roche School
pageCache.text:
Art
The Art room is a safe space for children to express themselves freely and individually. There are no mistakes: only creativity.
Our specialist Art teachers have high expectations of the children and their abilities. We use references from across diverse histories, cultures and identities and link the work to contemporary life. Every child has a voice in the Art room. This approach not only nurtures artistic skill but also equips our young artists with empathy, critical thinking and a strong sense of personal identity. We believe that Art is a communication and that it is a powerful tool for developing problem solving skills and supporting lateral thinking.
Pupils are regularly selected to show at the Royal Academy Young Artists’ Summer Exhibition and every June, Year 6 pupils proudly display their work at our own Roche School Year 6 Art Exhibition.
“I feel my art is really important. I am very proud of the work I do.”
“Art is my favourite subject and I love having the Art lessons as I learn so much.”
Music
We believe that music is a vital part of every child’s development, which is why we dedicate two full lessons each week to it.
Our weekly singing lessons, from Nursery to Year 6, are all about having fun while developing a true sense of musicality. Children learn to sing with clarity, expression and rhythm and their passion is simply outstanding. In our Music lessons, we journey through a world of musical styles—from early music to modern-day hits. We teach children to read music, understand rhythm, and even use sol-fa to develop pitch.
Children get hands-on experience by learning the recorder in Years 3 and 4 and the ukulele in Years 5 and 6. For those who want to explore further, we have a variety of extracurricular clubs, including orchestra and choirs, as well as individual tuition in a range of instruments.
“We love having Mr Gunther to play piano when we sing.”
“The ukeleles are so much fun! We got to write our own songs and play them.”
Drama
Drama, speech and performance are a particular strength of The Roche School. We believe in the power of drama to make learning interactive and memorable and use drama in lessons across the curriculum, allowing children to explore the perspectives of different characters through exercises such as hot-seating and conscience alleys. Pupils’ understanding of setting, plot and mood are expanded with the use of living landscapes and freeze-frames.
Every pupil participates in their annual year group play, performing in front of a packed house. The only exception is Year 5, when pupils are deeply ensconced in 11+ exam preparation and can instead opt-in to participate in the Coram Shakespeare Festival, where they get the chance to perform one of Shakespeare’s plays before a fresh audience at a real theatre.
“I love doing Drama because you can feel like you are in a different world.”
“I adore Drama because it is a fun way to be in a character’s shoes.”

Added Extras
It’s these added extras that bring each subject to life, make them feel relevant to our young people, powerfully engage their interest and provide them with a deeper understanding of the world around them.
Trips and Excursions
From participating in a mock trial at the Royal Courts of Justice, to learning to sword fight at a Macbeth workshop at The Globe Theatre, to perfecting the snowplough on the ski trip to France – these joyous experiences are how happy memories of our school days are made.
Excellent Facilities
We have a beautifully extensive library in our main building and Years 5 and 6 additionally benefit from their own dedicated library spaces. Our three computer suites, sprung-floor dance studio, in-house pottery kiln, raised stage and performance space and in-house kitchen all enrich our pupils’ daily experience of school life.
Our use of top-quality facilities enriches our pupils’ learning experience: easy access to the playing fields and tennis courts of Wandsworth Park, the 33m swimming pool we enjoy using in nearby Putney, and of course the wild spaces of Wimbledon Common and Richmond Park where our children enjoy regular Forest School lessons.
A rich curriculum fosters a love of learning and sets our pupils up for success.

What do we mean when we talk about ‘expert teaching’? Every teacher in our school is a knowledgeable, thoughtful and curious practitioner with excellent pedagogical skills, but we define expert teachers as those who have a high level of knowledge and skill in a particular subject area which goes beyond general teaching qualifications. This is different from the traditional primary school model where a single teacher is a “generalist” who teaches all subjects to one class.
Our subject specialists typically have a degree or advanced qualification in the specific subject they teach, providing them with in-depth knowledge that they can share with their colleagues, enabling connections to real-world applications and offering a richer learning experience for children. Having an expert teacher on each of our subject teams ensures that we are well-equipped to challenge high-achievers and provide extra support to pupils who need it.
Subject Specialists
Director of Sport, Tyrone Pugh, has a BA in Sports Psychology. He was Head of Sport in a secondary school in South Africa before taking up his first Director of Sport role in a preparatory school in North London. He joined The Roche School as Director of Sport in September 2024.
Director of Music, Katie Woodward, studied cello at the Royal College of Music under Margaret Moncrief and Alexander Boyarsky. She set up “The Truman Quartet” whilst there and performed for many functions, including for HRH Prince Charles at Highgrove, St James’s Palace and Clarence House. Besides this, she has won a county music scholarship, made several television appearances, and performed at the Queen Elizabeth Hall. Katie leads our junior, senior and chamber choirs, in additional to teaching music at our school.
Head of Art, Susie Prus, completed a foundation course at Chelsea School of Art, and an art degree and MA at Goldsmiths where she was taught by acclaimed artist Marina Abramovic. Alongside teaching at The Roche School, she has worked at Leighton House, been interviewed on BBC Radio 4, and she teaches at Putney High School.
Drama Lead, Melanie Parrish, is an experienced secondary English teacher who studied English Literature at University College London. Melanie was trained by the Coram Shakespeare national schools drama programme and has led our school’s successful participation in this festival for seven years. She is proud to have fostered a love of acting in Roche alumnus Aristou Meehan, who went on to star in the Wes Anderson film ‘Asteroid City’.
Maths Specialist Dr Alex Leithes has a PHD in Astrophysics from Queen Mary, University of London. He taught at Godolphin and Latymer School before joining us to specialise in Maths teaching.
Spanish Specialist, Vanessa Mieville, is a Doctor of Philosophy from Royal Holloway College, London University. Prior to training as a primary teacher she was Executive Manager of a Language Club franchise. Fluent in both Spanish and French, she had extensive language teaching experience before becoming a class teacher.
Head of English, Leanda Reeves, has a degree in Hispanic Studies from the University of Manchester, where she specialised in Medieval Spanish and Latin American Literature, alongside studying Spanish and Portuguese. With a PGCE from Goldsmith’s College, Leanda has experience of teaching A level and GCSE Spanish, prior to becoming a primary school teacher. Before joining The Roche School, Leanda was Head of English at Hurlingham School.
Lower School Lead, Kate Wiffen, holds a BA (Hons) in Early Primary Education and is a specialist in the teaching of children aged 3-7 years. Kate is a fully qualified and highly skilled Forest School teacher with many years of experience in teaching both Early Years and Key Stage One across a number of diverse educational settings.
Head of 11+, Gina Gent, has fostered excellent relationships with senior schools in London, Surrey and beyond over the course of several years. She has gained a high level of expertise in the ever-changing 11+ exam landscape and is perfectly positioned to support pupils in managing the transition to their chosen secondary schools.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our History | Private School Wandsworth | Roche School
pageCache.text:
1983
Mrs Roche’s Coaching Establishment was founded and welcomed five children to the home of Dr and Mrs Roche in West Kensington. Mrs Roche had an academic background in literature and languages and set out the founding principle of offering a ‘thorough education in a homely environment’. Morning lessons were followed by swimming, Art, cultural excursions and even ice-skating.
1988
Mrs Roche’s school was popular, with pupils winning places at some of London’s top senior schools and the school roll quickly expanded. This prompted a move to its current location in Wandsworth, where it officially became The Roche School. Dr Roche joined the teaching staff, bringing with him a love of Maths and Science. Excursions to the ice-rink were replaced with roller-skates in the playground. Indeed, pupils briefly campaigned to be allowed to wear their roller skates all day long.
2022
The Roche School now boasted a roll of over 200 pupils aged 2 to 11 and was firmly established in the Southwest London independent schools sector. September 2022 saw the introduction of an optional Spanish immersive stream running alongside the traditional English language curriculum. While English and Maths were still taught in English, pupils opting to explore bilingual learning were now able to enjoy learning History, Geography, Science, Religious Studies, Sport and more through the medium of Spanish.

How Does Wraparound Care Work At The Roche School?
What Does Our After-School Club Offer?
Our after-school provision is provided by Junior Adventures Group, which runs multi-activity clubs every day throughout the academic year. These include sports, creative sessions, games, crafts, and more, all aligned with our “Whole Child” philosophy to ensure fun, supportive and developmental enrichment.
A snack is provided for all children attending.
How Do I Book Wraparound Care?
Bookings are made via the Junior Adventures Group platform. Parents can sign their children up for the sessions they need in advance. A free trial session is offered as a way to introduce children to the club environment.
Why Choose Our Wraparound Care Programme?
High Quality Wraparound Care
Junior Adventures Group wraparound care after school offers a fun and enriching experience every day throughout the academic year, providing working parents with flexible childcare solutions during term time that children love to attend. From sports and games to crafts and creative sessions, every one of our multi-activity-based programmes is underpinned by our Whole of Child approach, meaning each child is inspired and supported to flourish through fun, safe, sociable experiences beyond the classroom. A healthy snack is served daily.

Early years learning at The Roche School is in line with the national Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum and further enriched by thoughtful integration of the Montessori Approach.
Pupils in our Nursery classes enjoy lively exploration of seven key areas of learning:
We are proud of our strong academic record and our Nursery pupils work towards and often beyond the Government’s Early Learning Goals through a combination of free-flow, play-based learning and engaging and specific teaching sessions. We track and observe each child’s progress closely and introduce reading books as soon as children are ready. Numbers, counting and the foundations of Maths are explored using tactile, practical resources which ensures that every child is engaged and challenged.

Safeguarding is of utmost importance and is a vital shared responsibility across our school community. Safeguarding training and support is led by our Designated Safeguarding Lead, who holds overall responsibility for this essential function. All staff and visitors play an important part in promoting the welfare of children and we ensure everyone understands their role in keeping pupils safe. Our approach is grounded in the national statutory guidance document, Keeping Children Safe in Education, and focuses on:
We work proactively to help children understand how to stay safe — online, in public spaces, and in everyday life. Our pupils are encouraged to speak up and know that their concerns will be treated with care, respect, and urgency.
The Roche School’s safeguarding policies are regularly reviewed and are fully embedded in daily school life. We value strong partnerships with parents and carers — your concerns and insights are always welcome.
If you have a safeguarding concern, please contact a member of our safeguarding team.
Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL): Louise Gilmartin (safeguarding@therocheschool.com)
Safeguarding at The Roche School is not just about protection — it is about building a community where every child can feel safe, grow with confidence, and reach their full potential.

pageCache.pageTitle: Spanish | Private School London | Roche School
pageCache.text:
Our unique Spanish immersive afternoons offer a dynamic, real-world approach to language learning, where children are taught a wide range of subjects from science and geography to art and sport in Spanish.
Spanish is embedded naturally across the curriculum while maintaining strong foundations in core subjects taught in English.
How does it work?
English in the morning
Spanish in the afternoon
Praise from the Spanish Embassy
We are delighted to report that our approach to Spanish language learning has the approval of the Spanish Embassy in London. In 2025, the Spanish Embassy’s education advisor, María Luisa Martínez, said that “The Roche School stands out as a remarkable institution” and that the “dedication and excellence of the teaching staff [is] evident in their well-prepared and engaging lessons, filled with creative topics that genuinely captivated the students.” Ms Martinez was impressed by our pupils’ “high level of Spanish, as they confidently followed the lessons in the language.”
University College London researchers have also been studying how the impact of bilingual learning has impacted our pupils.
Gaining a qualification in Spanish
By the time pupils are in Year 6, children demonstrating a high level with Spanish will be invited to prepare for the international A1 DELE exam for young learners if they are ready to do so. This is the first level of the Diplomas de Español como Lengua Extranjera (DELE) examinations offered by the Instituto Cervantes on behalf of the Spanish Ministry of Education and Vocational Training.
Spanish is for everyone
What if your child has no prior knowledge of Spanish, or your family has no connection to the Spanish language? Well, then, your child will be in good company. You may be interested to learn that many families who choose the Spanish immersive experience for their children have no prior links to Spanish. They recognise the benefits of bilingual learning and want to give their child the advantage of Spanish proficiency at an early age.
Our results show that children who have benefited from the Spanish immersive experience enjoy the same high level of results in English phonics, spelling, reading and writing as their peers. There is no downside to pursuing the Spanish immersive option: only upside.
What are you waiting for?
FAQs
How much of the curriculum is taught in Spanish?
The Spanish immersion classes hold morning lessons (Maths and Literacy) in English. Afternoons involve British Curriculum-based lessons taught in Spanish wherever possible. The lessons we deliver in Spanish include Art, History, Geography, Computing and Science.
Is The Roche School suitable for children who do not speak Spanish at home?
Absolutely! We have no language requirements for pupils or parents. We recognise that all children have unique backgrounds and that they may not have had access to Spanish previously. Initially, the focus is on simple communication with gesture, song and pictures, and on classroom vocabulary. We regularly assess the children’s Spanish levels to meet their needs.
Will learning in two languages affect my child’s English development?
The research shows that being exposed to more than one language has a positive impact on the brain.
Do pupils achieve fluency in Spanish?
The aim is to expose the pupils to Spanish as much as possible, whilst being aware that they will not become fluent due to our context.
Who teaches the Spanish elements of the curriculum?
Pupils are taught by one of our experienced teachers with in-depth Spanish knowledge.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Wellbeing | Nursery London | Roche School
pageCache.text:
A strong sense of wellbeing provides the foundation from which children can learn, develop and flourish. By embedding wellbeing into our daily practice and routines, we create an environment where kindness, respect and a culture of belonging can develop naturally.
We recognise that wellbeing encompasses much more than physical health. It includes children’s emotional, social and mental wellbeing, helping them to develop resilience, self-confidence and a strong sense of self. Children are encouraged to express their feelings openly and confidently, helping them to develop emotional awareness. Through guided discussions, reflection and age-appropriate activities, they learn to recognise, understand and manage their emotions in a positive and constructive way. The children are supported to build friendships, work collaboratively and develop the social skills that will support them in Nursery and as they progress through the school.
Outdoor play and physical activity are also key aspects of our approach to wellbeing. We ensure the children experience regular opportunities for active play and meaningful engagement with the natural environment fostering positive mental wellbeing. We encourage children to be curious and adventurous and to develop connections with the world around them. Our daily routines are designed to provide consistency and stability, helping children feel confident and settled. We also promote healthy eating, good personal care habits and opportunities for rest, supporting the children’s overall physical well being.
By working closely with families, we ensure that every child’s individual needs are understood and supported, creating a strong and consistent approach to well being both at Nursery and at home.
We are proud to provide an inclusive environment where children feel happy, valued and inspired to learn every day. It’s important to us that your child feels safe and happy every day.

How Does The Roche School Support Every Child’s Wellbeing?
What Is ‘The Roche Approach’ To Wellbeing And Values?
At the heart of our community is The Roche Approach – a simple, memorable way to express our school’s values:
This framework guides both children and adults in how we treat one another, shaping our ethos of kindness and consideration. Pupils are regularly recognised for demonstrating these values, with weekly assemblies celebrating those whose conduct exemplifies The Roche Approach. It is not just a motto – it’s a way of thinking, learning and being that enriches life throughout the school.
What Is ‘Room At The Roche’ And How Does It Support Pupils?
Room at The Roche is our wellbeing drop-in facility-a small room with a big heart, located in Hut 5 of the playground and staffed by our dedicated pastoral care team. Open during playtimes and lunchtimes, it offers pupils a safe, welcoming space to talk through any worries – from friendship challenges and exam stress to family changes or personal concerns.
Conversations held in Room at The Roche are confidential, but if appropriate and with the child’s consent, staff may reach out to parents for further support. The school also works closely with external professionals and therapists to ensure every pupil receives the right level of care.
Most often, a chat and a cuddle are all it takes to help a pupil feel calm, cared for, and ready to enjoy their day again.
